summary: Washington's enacted AI laws are about companion chatbots and deepfakes (adjacent), but AG Nick Brown signed the September 2026 multistate letter warning of potentially existential risk and urging Congress to keep AI under human control.

items.title: HB 2225 — AI companion chatbots
items.text: Requires AI disclosure, self-harm protocols and bans sexual content and manipulative engagement with minors; effective January 1, 2027.

items.title: 26-AG letter to Congress on frontier AI
items.text: Brown joined AGs urging federal frontier-AI oversight, saying inaction risks potentially existential harm.

profile.headline: Washington is studying data centers and AI more than it is regulating them: a big data center bill died in 2026, while three narrower AI laws passed.

sections.text: Gov. Bob Ferguson's Executive Order 25-05 (February 2025) created a Data Center Workgroup, which reported eight recommendations in December 2025. In March 2026 Ferguson signed three AI laws: HB 1170 (provenance or watermarking for AI-generated content), HB 2225 (companion chatbots, with protections for minors) and SSB 5886 (digital-likeness rights). A 19-member state AI task force released its final report in July 2026.

Quincy is the center of Washington's data center industry, with 53 facilities totalling about 1,073 MW; Microsoft runs 27 of them and Sabey 7. Data centers raised Quincy's assessed value to more than $6.1 billion in 2025 and pay 57% of its property tax. HB 2515, a comprehensive bill to regulate large data centers, passed the House 51-41 in 2026 but died in the Senate.

Seattle's City Council advanced a data center moratorium, with key votes scheduled for early June 2026 after grassroots campaigning. Opponents also organized a protest at an AI expo in Wenatchee in 2026.

The University of Washington launched AI@UW in February 2026, funded by a $10 million gift from Charles Simonyi in November 2025 and led by vice provost Noah Smith. The Allen School lists AI safety among its seven areas of AI work, and in September 2026 UW researchers including Franziska Roesner and Smith published a Q&A on AI risk.

Sen. Maria Cantwell (D), ranking member of Senate Commerce, led the July 2025 effort that removed a 10-year moratorium on state AI laws from the budget bill by a 99-1 vote. She later criticized the president's AI executive order for "overly broad preemption" that threatens states over protections against AI fraud, scams and deepfakes.
